comment_short: Evidence does not sufficiently support the strength of the main claims
action_taken: Endpoint hierarchy revised: navigation degradation promoted to primary, rotation demoted to mechanistic secondary. Disclosed as a post hoc revision.
result: Addressed. Rotation reported in full at p={{a1.rot.p_paired}} (primary, paired Wilcoxon; Holm {{a1.rot.holm}}) with the unpaired p={{a1.rot.p_unpaired}} alongside in every table and rho quoted with its 95% CI; not softened. The limitation is stated by the interval rather than a power simulation: Hodges-Lehmann {{a1.rot.hl}} with 95% CI [{{a1.rot.hl_lo}}, {{a1.rot.hl_hi}}], a lower bound about a quarter of the point estimate, so the effect is detected but its magnitude is poorly constrained at n={{cfg.n_seeds}} (C15). Rotation is a SECONDARY endpoint: the primary claim is navigation degradation, which no paired-versus-unpaired question touches.

where: CORRECTIONS.md C11; Section V; Results Table 1

comment_short: 1. No baseline comparison; "Benchmark" claim unsupported
action_taken: Open-loop always-advance control run on both retained anatomies at the operator arms' own simulation timestep, over {{floor.dt001_reps}} repetitions of the full seed list. "Benchmark" removed from title and positioning; the environment is described as a controlled instrument and the trivial floor as its control condition. No random policy was run.
where: Results §3.1; Table 1; Methods §2.4; CORRECTIONS.md C22; response letter §1.8 and R1.1
result: Addressed, and it went decisively against us. The open-loop control reaches target in {{floor.dt001_a1_k}}/{{floor.dt001_a1_n}} A1 and {{floor.dt001_a2_k}}/{{floor.dt001_a2_n}} A2 episodes - {{floor.dt001_a1_pct}}% of both - so the task requires no visual information. The operator reached target in {{a1.success_wo}}/{{cfg.n_seeds}} (wire-only) and {{a1.success_ov}}/{{cfg.n_seeds}} (overlay) on A1. Our first answer to this comment reported a floor of roughly half to two-thirds with a speed dependence and a reachability probe; all of it was measured at a timestep no study arm used and is withdrawn (C22). No test is run between the control and an operator arm.

comment_short: 4. Report a multiple-comparison correction
action_taken: Holm applied as primary, Bonferroni also reported. Full multiplicity table with confirmatory vs exploratory flags.
result: Addressed. Confirmatory family DECLARED as two members (A1, A2); A3 is excluded from Results and therefore from the family, and is given no adjusted p anywhere. A1 Holm p={{a1.rot.p_paired}}; A2 Holm p={{a2.rot.holm}} on the primary paired test (Bonferroni {{a1.rot.bonferroni}} and {{a2.rot.bonferroni}}), with unpaired values tabulated beside them and not adjusted over. Removing A3 did not ease the correction, and this is computed rather than asserted: both Holm values are identical under a two- or three-member family; only Bonferroni moves (A1 {{a1.rot.bonferroni}} vs {{a1.rot.bonferroni_if3}}). We also declined the opposite move - declaring three while reporting two would have overstated the burden in our favour at no cost.

comment_short: 3a. Rotation comparison used an unmatched Mann-Whitney on a matched design
action_taken: Replaced with Wilcoxon signed-rank on seed-matched pairs (C2), which REMAINS the primary test. We then tested the premise the objection rests on: the simulator seed does not propagate to outcomes at all (7h), and the within-pair correlation is rho={{rho.a1.frot}} (95% CI {{rho.a1.frot_lo}} to {{rho.a1.frot_hi}}) on A1 and undefined on A2 (wire_only arm constant). We briefly made the unpaired test primary on that basis (C13) and then reversed it (C14): at n={{cfg.n_seeds}} that interval shows pairing is not demonstrably helping, NOT that pairing is unjustified, which is too weak a basis for a {{hist.fold_improvement}}-fold change in the headline p-value. Unpaired reported alongside in every table.
where: CORRECTIONS.md C2/C13/C14; PRESPEC.md §9; Phase 4; Phase 7h/7i; Results
result: Addressed. Primary stays the matched test the reviewer asked for: A1 p={{a1.rot.p_paired}}, A2 p={{a2.rot.p_paired}}; unpaired alongside (A1 p={{a1.rot.p_unpaired}}, A2 p={{a2.rot.p_unpaired}}); conclusion identical under either test on both anatomies. The intermediate position was the one more favourable to us and we abandoned it on the imprecision of the estimate, not its direction.
